overview: This file brings together wartime and early postwar records on Japan’s overseas intelligence, propaganda, influence, and military-advisory activities. Its contents range from public allegations and tentative security warnings to detailed classified investigations: inquiries into Toyohiko Kagawa’s alleged broadcasts, surveillance of suspected Spanish and Filipino collaborators, reports on Japanese intelligence networks in Europe and China, and extensive biographies of military attaché Makoto Onodera and his associates. Later records concern alleged agents and advisers in postwar East Asia, especially Eijiro Yoshimoto, Lieutenant General Saito, and American propagandist Posey Wellington Reeves. A final group of telegrams about Gösta Guston and SKF broadens the file to questions of corporate connections, German assets, travel, and legal immunity.
interest: Shows U.S. efforts to reconstruct Japan's overseas networks, with inconclusive Kagawa inquiries versus the Reeves case.
